utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Cetina, I would like you to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you gave yesterday at the beginning of your testimony that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Misetic, are you ready to cross-examine Mr. Cetina?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic will now cross-examine you. He's counsel for Mr. Gotovina. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Cetina.

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to take you back to some answers that you gave yesterday to questions posed to you by Mr. Kay, and referring to transcript page 23.398, beginning at line 20. And you were asked about preparations that -- whether preparations had been made as a result of a meeting on the 3rd of August in Zagreb that Mr. Moric had called. And you said that you returned to Zadar, gathered the members of your specialist team, informed them of the imminent operation, and told them that we should get prepared for the return to that territory. And then the next question on the next page: "Was there any planning done in advance for the situation of check-points or areas of patrol?" And your answer was: "No, our primary objective was to reach the location and to get settled in the police building." And if could show you a document --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, this is P493, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: As you'll see on your screen, this was an order issued by Mr. Moric on the 3rd of August to the attention of police administration chiefs. And the Zadar-Knin Police Administration is one of the addressees of the order. And then it orders co-operation with the military police. And if you look through the order, there are specific tasks issued to establish contacts with the military police. The second point under point 1 is -- sorry, it's to establish contacts with the military police in your police administration and agree on harmonised action in the implementation of tasks. At the demarcation lines, establish check-points jointly with the military police. It tells you what to do with journalists, to -- and the next point is establish law and order, ensure smooth traffic flow in liberated settlements to organise joint patrols. The last one on the first page in the English says: At the intersections of important roads establish joint check-points. If we turn the page, what to do with refugees. Point 2 is a point on treatment of captured members of paramilitary units. Now, my first question is: Do you recall receiving this order on the 3rd of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I saw it on the 3rd of August. Perhaps we should look at the document itself, but it may have reached me on the 4th or the 5th. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, did you do any preparations on any of the items that were sent in this order in terms of planning for where check-points would be? Did you establish communication with the military police in your area of responsibility prior to Operation Storm beginning?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that we established contacts. I said yesterday that the primary objective was to reach the locations where we were supposed to set up police stations, whereas all these tasks it was understood would follow afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me turn your attention to another document, Mr. Cetina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is, Mr. Registrar, 65 ter 4414.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This was another order issued on the 3rd of August to, amongst others, to yourself, the administration chief of the Zadar-Knin Police Administration. And in this order Mr. Moric advises you or orders you, I should say, to -- at 0300 hours on 4 August to ban all civilian traffic on the following roads --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- sorry, I should say that first entry was along the road M2 from Zadar to the Maslenica Bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we scroll to the very top, please in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sorry, and Prizna. It goes on in the next paragraph to say: "At precisely 0400 hours ..." there is a ban of civilian traffic on several roads. And it talks about where civilian traffic should be directed, et cetera. Do you recall receiving this order prior to the commencement of Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember; however, it would only be logical that we did receive it and act upon it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. President, I ask that 65 ter 4414 be marked and I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will become Exhibit P2654.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P2654 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Sorry, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it should receive a D number. That's -- I followed Mr. Registrar as I always do, but here perhaps it would have been better to suggest a D number. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise for the error, Your Honours. It should be D1759.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We now admit into evidence D1759 I think it was.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, D1759.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And P2654 is vacated. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cetina, as a general matter, do you agree with me that the police had the authority to detain members of the Croatian army at check-points if, for example, they were found to have looted items in their possession; they were allowed to detain them and then they were supposed to call in the military police so that these individuals could be processed further in the military criminal justice system?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's all right in theory, but in practice, things were different.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, let's take a look at --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, 65 ter 1D2994, please. If we could show the witness the top of the page in the Croatian original, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'd ask you to peruse this document, Mr. Cetina. It's dated the 3rd of October, 1995, and it is a document authored by you. And it's a plan for a stake-out. And in the introduction you say that you have operative information in connection with the criminal offence of violence committed by three unknown perpetrators wearing Croatian army uniforms on the 3rd of October around 1330 hours against a victim named Andjelko Gambiroza, a Croat by nationality, in the manner that, while holding the above stated under gunpoint, the unknown persons ransacked his house and threatened him. And he must leave his home because if he didn't they would come back during the night, liquidate him, and take his cattle. For the purpose of preventing the criminal offence of violence from being committed against Mr. Andjelko Gambiroza and capturing the unknown perpetrators, the police department of the Zadar-Knin Police Administration brings the following: Implementation plan for a stake-out. And then you describe a plan or you order a plan. The stake-out would begin at 2200 hours on the 3rd of October and be carried out by a special police unit of the Zadar-Knin Police Administration and by military police members from the independent company of the 72nd MPs in Knin. The stake-out lasts until 0600 hours. You are to notify the victim that the stake-out is going to take place. Point 5 is reports on potential actions during the stake-out or observations which may be of interest are to be delivered to the commander of the Knin police station after the stake-out or, rather, surveillance has been included. "I hold the commander of the special police group or, rather, the commander of the Knin police station responsible for the implementation of the stake-out." Now, Mr. Cetina, this is an example where -- where unknown perpetrators potentially could, in fact, be members of the Croatian army. The police, nevertheless, had the ability to investigate the matter and then, depending on the outcome of or the identity of the perpetrators, if caught, either processed the individuals themselves or, if they turn out to be members of the Croatian army, to refer the matter to the military police for further prosecution. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The key here does not lie in the stake-out plan; rather, in who would carry out the plan. It was envisaged that the special units of the police and the military police would carry out the stake-out. And this is the key issue. The ordinary uniformed police were not able to carry out such acts. In addition to that, it says -- it doesn't say that it was members of the Croatian army who were the perpetrators; rather, it says that there are reasonable grounds to suspect that they might have worn HV uniforms. Let me repeat that the key does not lie in the drafting of the plan, because that's, of course, where the ordinary uniformed police would have a major role; rather, that the forces materialising the plan were different, and they're listed under number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, but, Mr. Cetina, first you agree with me that you would have had no authority to issue any order to the military police; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I could not have ordered the military police. I suppose that the plan was drafted at the level of the department chief, Mr. Bitanga, in co-operation with the military police. The plan does not say that we could have ordered the military police; rather, it's envisaged that the action, the operative action, would be carried out jointly by the civilian and the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I understand that. But what I'm suggesting to you is that, for example, the special police units that are referred to here are units under your command as the chief of the police administration, Zadar-Knin; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. However, let me repeat - and I stand by what I said - the involvement of the special police units and the military police force went along the lines of the fact that they were the only forces capable of confronting the individuals described at the outset, at the beginning of the plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. What I'm -- Mr. Cetina, if you look at paragraph 6 of the order, you say you are holding the commander of the special police group or, rather, the commander of the Knin police station responsible for the implementation of the stake-out. My only point to you is: Regardless of whether you're using the fundamental police, the basic police, or the special police unit, in terms of the MUP's side of this plan, the MUP had the authority to conduct a stake-out even where the unknown perpetrators were suspected to be members of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me try and clarify this. When it comes to the use of the military police, that's quite clear; however, when the use of the special police forces comes into play, the matter is quite different. The special police force was attached in a way - as far as I know - to the Croatian army for the purposes of Operation Storm. Therefore, before Operation Storm and after Operation Storm it was under the competence of the Zadar Knin-police administration. In this particular instance, the force went back under the command of the Zadar-Knin Police Administration. I presume as much because that would have been the general idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We'll continue on this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: But first if I can ask, Mr. President, that this exhibit be marked and I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the document can be admitted into evidence, but, Mr. Misetic, could you closely look at whether the translation is made with the accuracy we would think it should be. For example, the age of Mr. Gambiroza, in English he becomes rather young.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, we'll correct the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think he was born after the incident occurred from what I can see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Similarly, Mr. Kay, yesterday you quoted from D586, where you were kind enough to correct the translation, that is, "mobilisation" and "demobilisation." You corrected the incorrect translation the second time to the word "demobilizacija." You said, of course, that that's what is meant, and not "mobilisation" as we find in English. It was a -- not a final translation. We saw a lot of not final translations yesterday, and sometimes if we find such a clear mistake in translation the Chamber would very much appreciate if that whole document would be reviewed and would be made a full translation, rather than to expect that everyone now or even if there ever would be an appeal would immediately know where the translation is wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Registrar, this document, although a corrected version will be uploaded, would receive number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit Number D1760, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1760 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, if we could see, please, Exhibit D576.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Cetina, you saw this document yesterday. Mr. Kay asked you some questions about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is, again, your report back to Mr. Moric about statistics of crime taking place in the Zadar-Knin Police Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go to page 2 in the English. And we've lost the B/C/S. Unfortunately this is illegible in the B/C/S, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If you look at the paragraph that begins: "There are still some individual cases of house burning ..." That is the fourth paragraph in the Croatian version. "There are still some individual cases of house burning and removal of movable property by others than the owners on the entire liberated area. The perpetrators are, for the most part, uniformed HV personnel, while civilians are less frequently involved as perpetrators. "On-site investigations are performed independently by the civilian police without the presence of the military police." Then you give statistics: "Between 20 August and 31 August ... a total of 55 on-site investigations were carried out: 47 on-site investigations for burnings and eight on-site investigations for abstraction of movable property. "Where crimes have been committed, an investigation is launched. "During the reporting period, nine perpetrators in HV uniforms were identified. No individuals were reported for misuse of HV uniforms." My question to you is: Your report indicates that the Zadar-Knin Police Administration is conducting on-site investigations independently without the presence of the military police. How were you able to identify nine perpetrators in HV uniforms of the crimes that were committed?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me repeat again. The information contained herein is summary information that was sent from the police stations out in the field. The information is based on data which could not perhaps be used as such to be delivered to the republican prosecutor's office. They were the result of what the police on the ground was able to observe. This does not necessarily mean that we processed as many cases in our dealings with the prosecutor's offices. I repeat, these are -- the data contained therein is summary information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yeah, but that's not what my question concerned. The MUP was, in fact, investigating crimes and, within the context of those investigations, was competent to identify HV members as the perpetrators if, in fact, that's what they found; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can say that the term "members" was used probably because Croatian army insignia seemed to have been recognised, but the report does not say per se that these were HV members that were identified. I don't have the text before me anymore. I can't refer to the exact portion. Perhaps this could be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's at the bottom, the last sentence on your screen in front of you in Croatian.

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I have nothing at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please check and --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now it's here. It's fine now. Thank you. Sorry, could you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me rephrase it. The MUP had general jurisdiction to investigate and identify -- investigate crime and identify the perpetrators of crime, including if the person was wearing an HV uniform; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in co-operation with members of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And that's not what this report says, Mr. Cetina. You specifically wrote that the "on-site investigations are performed independently by the civilian police without the presence of the military police." That's what the report says. Now, I'm asking you again: You had general jurisdiction to identify perpetrators of crime, even if the perpetrator was wearing an HV uniform, irregardless of whether a military police member was present?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On-site investigations at crime scenes could have been performed by the civilian police, but a criminal investigation directed against HV members according to the Law on the Interior could only be carried out together with the military police, that is to say, such persons would be handed over to the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cetina, I don't want to play a semantics game with you, so let's make sure we are talking about the same thing, and I'll give you an example. The MUP has a check-point where there are no military policemen present, and yesterday Mr. Kay took you through several reports where you were complaining about the lack of military police at MUP check-points. On that check-point, a car with civilian licence plates comes up with three individuals in HV uniforms in it, with a trailer containing household items, televisions, refrigerators, et cetera. The MUP police at that check-point - you will agree with me - has the authority to stop that car; to identify those individuals; and, if it suspects that the goods on the trailer are stolen, to exclude them from traffic; detain them; call the military police, if in fact they are identified as active HV members; and then further processing would be conducted by the military police. That's how the system worked; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could agree. But in practice, it depended on the assessment of the police officers involved. They were supposed to estimate whether this could lead to a conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay, yesterday you were asked some questions about Mr. Moric's order of the -- I believe it was the 17th of August, where, in answer to the Presiding Judge, you referred to what the law was and what you were required to do under the law. And that's what I'm asking you right now. Under the law, the police was required to act as I described in my prior question; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Moric did require that. But the implementation of such orders was supposed to be in keeping with the Law on the Interior and the Law on Criminal Procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me rephrase my question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I seek clarification of one of the previous answers. When Mr. Misetic gave you a picture of what could happen at a check-point, he asked whether that was how the system work, and you said: "I could agree. But in practice, it depended on the assessment of the police officers involved. They were supposed to estimate whether this could lead to a conflict." What kind of conflicts were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A conflict in the sense that such people could resist being identified. We discussed that yesterday. We insisted that at check-points, together with our police officers, there be the military police as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You would say that if the civilian police would take action against such a person under those circumstances, that whether or not to do that would depend on their estimate on whether those persons would accept such an intervention by the civilian police in the absence of the military police. Is that how I have to understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Cetina, it was simply left up to the perpetrators to decide how they wished to be processed or whether they wished to be processed, and you left it to the perpetrators to make the determination as to whether they would be apprehended or not?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation as such lasted for about a month and a half, during which there were possibilities of such rows. The risk period was about a month or a month and a half, during which we have to apply this type of approach in order to overcome the period.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, let's take it -- let's look at a concrete example.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could have Exhibit D660 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is a work order of the MUP from the 14th of August, and then the next page is the report of what these police officers actually did on the 14th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Point -- paragraph 1 of the report, it talk -- it says: "Vehicles, persons, and baggage, that is, items transported from and to Benkovac were checked. Approximately 20 vehicles were inspected, of which seven entered Benkovac with an appropriate permit, while the other civilian vehicles were driven by persons dressed in Croatian army uniforms, whose identity we verified and established that they were members of the Croatian army." If you look at paragraph 3: "At 11.30 hours we prevented the unlawful transport of tractors (i.e. without any documents) by three persons dressed in Croatian army uniforms, who were driving three tractors, two trailers, and a cultivator with trailer from the direction of Benkovac. These persons were kept until the arrival of the military police and then returned along with the stolen vehicles back to Benkovac." That is how the police was supposed to act; isn't that correct, Mr. Cetina? If you encounter members of the Croatian army looting and you stopped them at a check-point, you detain them and wait for the military police to arrive?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: One should applaud to the police. I think we fared rather well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, then let's look at another report of yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: D581, if we could have that on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is your report. Again, you were shown this document yesterday. It's the 12th of September. It's a report to Mr. Moric.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if we go to the bottom -- to page 2 in the English, please, and the fourth paragraph in the Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "On-site investigations are performed independently or in co-operation with a civilian investigating judge without the presence of the military police. "Between 22 August and 10 September ... a total of 82 on-site investigations were carried out, of which 75 were related to burnings and seven to mining." Then the last paragraph is: "During the reporting period, there were no individuals reported for abuse of HV uniforms and 28 HV members have been identified as perpetrators." Now, once again, you, in fact, were conducting on-site investigations and identifying HV members as perpetrators of crimes without any co-operation from the military police; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could only respond to this question if I saw the case file of the 28 HV members and the crimes involved. It is only then that I could tell you who did what and in what way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, you're the author of this document, Mr. Cetina, so what were you conveying to Mr. Moric when you said that 28 HV members had been identified as perpetrators and that 82 total on-site investigations were carried out?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I just said, we forwarded summary reports. In order for me to be able to tell you who followed up these 28 cases, I would have to look into the cases individually. I did not see the files. People drafting the summary report had insight into that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, can you at least tell us what does it mean in your report when you report that "28 HV members have been identified as perpetrators"? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This should mean that if there was reasonable doubt of such persons having committed a crime, that the state attorney's office was notified.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So would you then agree with me -- or let me see if I can sum up what you're saying. As a legal matter, the MUP had the ability to act towards perpetrators in HV uniforms, but whether they did it in practice was a question of their own judgement?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Cetina, at page 8 of your OTP statement you discuss the issue of issuing documentation to persons who had lived in the occupied territory up until Operation Storm. And can you tell us, first of all a -- let's take the example of an ethnic Serb who lived in Knin and was born in Knin, but up until Operation Storm had never sought Croatian documentation. In the Croatian system, what was their status? In other words, until they actually applied for their identification papers, what -- were the persons there, formally speaking, Croatian citizens or persons who had the right to obtain Croatian citizenship?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Formally speaking, those persons were expected to lodge an application to obtain Croatian citizenship.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Until they lodged that application, do you know whose citizenship they had? In other words, when the Republika Srpska Krajina existed, do you know whose citizenship these individuals had?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, you're now focusing your question on the Republika Srpska Krajina period, whereas I wondered, if someone was born in 1980, being an ethnic Serb -- well, perhaps his birth being registered but that's being all -- whether what would be the citizenship of that person before the Republika Srpska Krajina came into existence. Is that something --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that was included in your question? I did not -- in your first question, I wasn't aware that you excluded it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, I was talking about the period from 1990 to 1995. So in -- I have a document that might assist the Court, which will -- I will either put questions to him or bar table it, Mr. President. This is 65 ter 1D3000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look at it, but I don't make it a secret to you that I would like to know what happened with citizenship since the birth of that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, I think, from 1980 to 1990, I think, we're all in agreement on whose citizenship they would have, I would assume. From 1990 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: From 1990 onwards, take a look at this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If -- because the original is so difficult to read, we received it from the Office of the Prosecutor, I have a hard copy for the witness if he prefers. But if he can read it on the screen, that's fine, and if he can read Cyrillic. Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And Mr. Cetina, you'll see Article 1 of the RSK Law on Citizenship says: "A citizen of the Republika Srpska Krajina has citizenship of the RSK." Article 2 says: "A citizen of the RSK is concurrently a citizen of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And then if we turn to page -- I'm sorry, if we call up 65 ter 1D3001.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Court participants are kindly requested to switch off the microphones which are not being used. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And then this is an amendment to the Law on Citizenship of the RSK that was passed on the 16th of October, 1993, with the termination of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia and its replacement with the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. The law was amended to state at Article 2 -- in Article 1 and Article 2 that the words "Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia" are replaced with the words "Federal Republic of Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. President, we -- and I'd ask then, under the Croatian system, but our position based on this would be that the individuals were citizens of the FRY in August of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: With respect to their status, Mr. Cetina, under the Croatian system after the conclusion -- or during and after the conclusion of Operation Storm I understand your answer to be that they are considered to be persons with the right to obtain Croatian citizenship, which isn't then consummated until they actually apply with the appropriate Croatian authorities to obtain that Croatian citizenship; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had the right to file an application.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, perhaps my mind is not quick enough to follow all this. You just showed us a piece of legislation which says that a citizen of the Republic of Serb Krajina is a citizen of the Republic of Serb Krajina. That's what the law says, isn't it? Which raises --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Two things, Mr. President, that was Article 1 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was the one and the second one that simultaneously was also a citizen of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, still -- but forgive me that it's still a puzzle. That still doesn't answer for me the question who is a citizen of the Republic of Serb Krajina. We know that if you're a citizen, that you have citizenship of the Republic of Serb Krajina. But that is the same as saying if you've got blue hair, you're among the blue-haired people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's Article 3, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we can go back to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the previous one. Yes, because then we saw this second law --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- which that the "Socialist Federal Republic" -- that terminology is replaced by "Federal Republic." But --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- as far as I remember, I saw already "Federal Republic of Yugoslavia" for obtaining your citizenship and not "Socialist."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, if we can go back to 65 ter 1D3000, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I would like to be able to follow exactly what we are looking at and what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You'll see, Mr. President, in Article 2 it refers to the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And then Article 3 defines who has the right to acquire citizenship of the RSK.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let me see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I should also add, Mr. President, how specifically, within each of those four categories, is then further elaborated upon in the subsequent text of the law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just perhaps - and I take it that there will be no great dispute about it - would you have to apply or would it be automatic? By origin, for example, or by birth on the territory, that sounds very much as if it would automatically apply once you're born there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The quickest way is to make it an exhibit so that I can read the whole of the document. And then, of course, my next question would be, We know that in all matters of nationality that it's not uncommon that one state says you're a national of my state on this and this and this basis but that another state might issue legislation which grants also citizenship of the other state. So this is the RSK legislation which we can go through. What was the existing Croatian legislation in terms of people of Serb ethnicity born on the territory of one of the former republics of the -- of Yugoslavia, that is, Croatia? Because I could imagine - I'm not saying it is, but it comes to my mind - that it could well be that obtaining citizenship of the RSK might not impress that much the Croatian authorities which would not even acknowledge the existence of such a state, let alone on the Croatian territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, it would not -- and if I may refer back to the cross-examination of Elisabeth Rehn we touched upon this a little bit in that cross-examination, Mr. President. Obtaining Croatian citizenship had nothing to do with their status under the Republika Srpska Krajina, which was an entity that Croatia never recognised in the first place. However, the issue was the persons who were born in the then-Socialist Republic of Croatia, had the right to obtain Croatian citizenship. The issue raised during Mrs. Rehn's cross-examination was, and I suspect the witness may know something about this, that the way you obtained it was you had to go to your local county where the register of births were kept, which was the only way the state had of knowing who actually was born on the territory of Croatia and who was not. Part of the problem which is now in evidence is that those were taken in the evacuation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the registers were not available anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do remember that. I do not have all the details of Mrs. Rehn's cross-examination immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. So from Croatia's perspective - and I think the witness could speak to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps he will.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Cetina, in terms of how -- let's take as an example an ethnic Serb in Knin on the 8th of August, so after Operation Storm, that person could prove their right to Croatian citizenship by, amongst other things, showing a copy of their birth documents in the registers which should have been in Knin at the time evidencing their birth in Knin. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. That would be a sufficient enough document for the police to serve as an identification of the individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And do you recall there being problems as a result of missing birth records, death records, marriage records, et cetera, that may have been taken by the RSK authorities when they left?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember the details. Anyhow, these are administrative matters, matters of state administration which I really cannot speak about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that 65 ter 1D3000 and 1D3001 be marked and I tender them into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, those will become Exhibit D1761 and D1762 respectively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I wonder, Mr. Misetic -- I wonder whether it would be wiser to separate the two or to keep them together as one exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you wish to make it more efficient we can make them one exhibit. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not only efficiency, also because they are related to some extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that at least prevents that we lose sight of another document related to the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could we assign the two documents one number, that would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, in that case both documents 1D3000 and 1D3001 will become Exhibit Number D1761.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1761 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cetina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mikulicic, are you ready to cross-examine Mr. Cetina? Mr. Cetina, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Mikulicic. Mr. Mikulicic is counsel for Mr. Markac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Cetina.

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I know that a lot of time has elapsed since the events that are at the centre of this case, and I know that the memory tends to fade, but please focus on answering my questions as best you can so that we can assist the Trial Chamber in establishing the actual state of affairs. On the 1st of January, 1995, you were appointed as chief of the Zadar-Knin Police Administration, were you not, Mr. Cetina?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Let me go back to your statement given to OTP investigators, which is now D1745, where you state, in relation to the powers that you had in terms of discipline within the military -- within the police administration, that they were regulated by the law. Can you tell us what sort of powers did you have as the administration chief in terms of enforcing the discipline among the employees of the police?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where there were grounds to suspect that policemen should be held liable in certain -- in terms of discipline because he had allegedly violated discipline, he would have been held responsible in terms of disciplinary responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We've heard already in this case that there were two forms of disciplinary offences: Minor and major. When it came to minor disciplinary breaches, were you entitled to pass down such -- such measures?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we had first-instance disciplinary court - and I should not have had the right to interfere with its dealings anyhow. My only power was to file a request for the initiation of a disciplinary procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Similarly, there was a system in place in case there was a major breach of discipline, but in that case, again, the disciplinary court would be the one to decide and to act pursuant to your request. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cetina, should it happen that a member of your police administration, a person identified, would be a suspect in relation to the commission of a crime and that an investigation was launched before the competent court, had you received notice of it, what sort of powers would you have in that respect?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a rule, where there is a certain degree of suspicion, a disciplinary procedure is to be launched, although this is a hypothetical question, but this is the way things should transpire in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I have another option that I would like to hear your explanation about. Should the -- there be a suspicion that an unidentified member of your police administration took part or had a part to play in the commission of a crime, who would be charged with the investigation procedure? Would it be you as administration chief or would there be somebody else envisaged under the law to carry out the investigation?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for the criminal investigation that would be the police; and for the judicial investigation, the court investigation, that would be the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us clarify one fact which I believe still remains unclarified and stems from your statement, the one that you gave to the Prosecution, D1745, page 3, where you speak of the special police units which were organised within your police administration. This was mentioned a moment ago. And you drew a distinction in terms of what sort of powers the special police units had in peacetime and in times of its use in combat operations such as, for instance, Operation Storm. Would you agree with me, Mr. Cetina, that these are two different sets of circumstances?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: It is true, is it not, that members of the special police who were engaged in combat activities during Operation Storm were outside of your jurisdiction and within the jurisdiction, in fact, of the Main Staff of the Croatian army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: However, where they were not engaged in combat activities but, rather, on duties within your police administration, duties that were of a peacetime character, then you were the one deciding about their engagement; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you for these answers. Mr. Cetina, we have just been discussing the issuance of documentation to the citizens who did not have documents and happened to find themselves in the territory of the Republic of Croatia, and I'm primarily referring here to the citizens of Serb ethnicity. Did you know whether there was any sort of discrimination employed by the state authorities issuing such documentation in respect of Serb citizens who applied for Croatian citizenship?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: When you say "no," do you want to say that there was no such discrimination or that you didn't know?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of it; and had I been, I would have most certainly opposed the practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you recall anyone ever addressing you or your subordinates in protest - and I'm referring to citizens of Serb ethnicities - in protest of a fact that in the documentation issuing a procedure they were discriminated against or dealt with in a way that was different to the treatment according to members of the Croat ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have document 3D04-1087.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cetina, let's move to a different topic now, that is to say the searches of the terrain which were widely used in the aftermath of Operation Storm. As you can see here, this is a letter sent by Assistant Minister Mr. Moric, Josko Moric, to various police administrations including yours on the 9th of August which states that it is presumed that elements of Chetnik units are on the run in the woods and that there is a possibility of them attacking the police, and that the instruction was that in such cases the sector of the special police force should be informed as a matter of urgency. Mr. Cetina, do you know whether there were such instances in practice where the straggling elements of Serb personnel were to be found in the Croatian territory hiding away from representatives of the Croatian authorities?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Under such circumstances, you did not - did you? - engage members of the ordinary uniformed police to deal with these matters; rather, on such cases you notified the special police forces. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because the ordinary uniformed police were not trained or equipped for such actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have this document entered into the evidence, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will become Exhibit D1762.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cetina, correct me if I'm wrong, you were aware of the fact that members of the special police, following the combat activities, took part in the searches of the terrain in the areas that were liberated?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up document 65 ter 5828.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cetina, I will show you a document which has to do with this issued. It will soon appear on the screen. This is a document sent by General Mladen Markac from the special police sector to the Gospic Split Military District, to the Knin Garrison, as well as to the chief of the Licko-Sinjska Police Administration and the chief of the Zadar-Knin Police Administration. The document informs them of the activities carried out in the searches of the terrain. Can you confirm, Mr. Cetina, that this was a way of searching the terrain in order to avoid certain unwanted situations that may involve the local population and the police force active in the area?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: May I tender this document into the evidence, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit Number D1763.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us move on to a different topic, i.e., sanitisation of the terrain. This was already discussed, and I do not wish to duplicate your testimony and waste Their Honours' time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask the Registrar to call up document D233.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In other words, this is a document that has already been admitted into evidence. An order on the conduct of sanitisation. And this is something that was sent to, among others, the Zadar-Knin Police Administration. And the procedure of sanitisation is described here in detail. Let me first ask you: Have you ever seen this order? Has it passed through your hands as have many other thousands of such documents?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in fact that's the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: At any rate, now that you're looking at it, can you recall that the exact procedure of sanitisation was set out in the first days of Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and this is in fact the way in which it was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look up document D601 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This is another document on the same issue. It has also been drafted by Assistant Minister Mr. Zidovec. The date is of the 7th of August, in other words two days later. This document was sent to your police administration too. The document states that the chiefs of the police administrations have, based on assessments, a duty to pass decisions engaging the civilian protection, public utility companies and others as a matter of urgency in order to engage in sanitisation. Do you recall whether you used the services of the public utility company, such as the street cleaning, fire brigade, et cetera, in the duties relating to sanitisation?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection we did, although we needed to get more personnel in than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In the course of the sanitisation of the terrain where dead bodies were detected, members of the crime police force within your administration were involved; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Is it true that where a trained policeman would establish by examining the body that there was a suspicion of a crime of foul play, was his duty -- or rather, let me ask you: What was his duty in that case?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: His duty was to assess what the matter at hand was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: If he were to establish that there was foul play, in other words, murder, what was his obligation as a crime investigation policeman?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the degree of suspicion was high enough in his assessment, the crime investigation police was supposed to be notified.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What would follow such a notice?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the degree of suspicion is high enough, if that's the sort of assessment made, then the Law on Criminal Procedure was supposed to be applied.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Let me translate your answer into laymen's terms. Does it mean that in that case a team would be formed which would conduct an on-site investigation, and where it would be established that a crime was committed, a criminal procedure would follow?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are in fact activities as part of the inquiry or investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we next please see 65 ter document 4564.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cetina, based on this instruction of Assistant Minister Mr. Zidovec to mobilise civil protection forces for which chiefs of the police administrations were responsible, I wanted to show you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I am advised that this is already D348, so I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- I wanted to show you a document you sent out on the 8th of August to the Ministry of the Interior in which you report on the carried out mobilisation of civilian protection forces as well as on the number of corpses that were found in the territory of this other Knin police administration. Looking at the document, could you recall those particular events?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We sent a number of similar documents to the ministry, but yes it was always in this format.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wanted to enter this document into the evidence, but obviously it is already in the evidence, so I have no further --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then there is no need to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. And I'm sorry for this mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cetina, I thank you for your answers. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, that concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mikulicic. Ms. Mahindaratne, looking at the clock, I think it would be wiser to invite you to start your cross-examination after the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have a break, Mr. Cetina. We'll resume at ten minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, I was informed that you would need another three minutes. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you. [Interpretation] Registrar, could we please have 2D00545.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cetina, although I said I concluded your cross-examination, in the meantime I came across an important document concerning a disciplinary proceedings. And I would just require your comment after you were able to see the document. As you can see, this is a request to initiate a disciplinary procedure. We cannot see it here, but you signed it. You submitted this application against an employee of the police administration by the name of Roko Soric because on the 31st of August he was found driving a vehicle without registration plates. Do you recall that event?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Briefly, could you describe the situation to us given that you were the person who actually found the person committing the disciplinary breach?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall this case in which I personally acted against that person who was a police member when I arrived in Knin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you can assist us. We have some problems with the transcript, I understand. So, Mr. Mikulicic, could you please explain in your language to Mr. Cetina that we have to wait for a second until we have resolved this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cetina, there seems to be a problem, technical glitch, with the transcript. We'll have to wait until that is resolved. Therefore, please do not start answering yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Hopefully a re-start of the system will help us out. If not, we'll see. If no one speaks, we'll never find out whether the system is working again. This is also the moment to remember that we are lost without a transcriber and a functioning system. Mr. Mikulicic, could you please start again where the system was not functioning anymore. You asked for 2D00545 to be on the screen. Could you please re-start at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cetina, I will repeat my question for the record, at least the part of it that was not recorded. You see that this is a request for the initiation of disciplinary proceedings submitted by you. I wanted to ask you whether you recall that event as an example of the disciplinary measures that were at the disposal of the police administrations?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You, as the chief of the police administration, submitted this request to initiate disciplinary proceedings, based on which the disciplinary court was supposed to act; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now kindly ask the Registrar to turn the next page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We can see that this is a decision by which the police member is being suspended from duty during the disciplinary proceedings. This is actually a suspension from work; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: As a part of that suspension, the police badge and the police uniform are being seized of the policeman. That was one part of the disciplinary measures; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now move to the next page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We can see here that the proceedings were initiated by the first police station in Knin for the crime of theft. It seems that there were reasonable grounds to believe that he had committed that crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a set of documents under the one number, and it show ups the procedure in the disciplinary matter referring to Mr. Soric Roko. [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the Registrar to move a step further. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cetina, you see this is a letter of the Knin police station sent to the chief of the police administration in which it is stated that there were grounds to believe that Mr. Roko Soric committed the crime of? aggravated theft from Article 126 and that it is asked that disciplinary proceedings be instituted. In parallel --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And if we can go to the next page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: -- we see that the police measure of seizure of objects is being implemented, that is to say his side-arm, his rifle, and his badge were being taken away?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Another part of the document, please. This is a page of the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can see, Mr. Cetina, that this is a receipt of temporary seizure of certain objects, the official side-arm, rifle, and police badge were being taken from Mr. Roko Soric. This was part of standard procedure; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And if we go further, we see that there is another receipt --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: If I could ask the Registrar to go one step further, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another confirmation of temporary confiscation. The vehicle that he was found driving was also seized, and you were the person who found him driving that vehicle. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: If I could ask the Registrar to go one step further, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Finally, the last document in the batch is a note of receipt in which we can see that certain objects were seized, including the official side-arm, rifle, and ammunition. Those items were seized by the police station. Was this standard procedure during the relevant period of time in cases of disciplinary breaches or offences committed by members of the police administration?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less this is the procedure. The seized items included the rifle and the ammunition which were not involved in the commission of the crime, if there was a crime at the end. The vehicle was seized as well, although it may have been ascertained later on that there was no theft of vehicle. I believe the procedure was concluded by simply initiating a disciplinary procedure against the employee for driving a vehicle without traffic -- without plates.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Is this part of standard procedure as well?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: May I, please, enter this document into the evidence, Your Honour. That is to say, the set of documents. Your Honour, I was just advised that I spoke in vain. Could I have this document entered into the evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, series of documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will become Exhibit D1764.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour for additional time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Mikulicic, we started with the seizure and the reporting and serious reasons to believe that the four -- found may not be the one belonging to the police officer. Any final decisions because the witness tells us that he may have been driving without his licence plates on his car. Do you think --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's all we've got. Maybe we could ask the witness; maybe he remembers that specific incident --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, he said something about that it was his recollection that it may have been just driving without licence plates. But we could ask you, perhaps, Mr. Cetina. Do you have any recollection on this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it established that the car belonged to the police officer, or was anything established about ownership of the car in which he was found driving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember that I pulled him over and identified him. As for any follow-up procedure concerning the vehicle and the objects, that is something I'm not familiar with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, I think you said something about it - let me just check. You said: "Although it may have been ascertained later on that there was no theft of the vehicle which is" -- and you said: "I believe the procedure was concluded by simply initiating a disciplinary procedure against the employee for driving a vehicle without traffic -- without licence plates." Of course, I'm more or less asking you now on the basis of what you believe this. And you say: "As for any follow-up procedure concerning the vehicle and the objects, that is something I'm not familiar with." Although, you suggested at least some familiarity, that is, that the whole issue of theft was not further pursued.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't trying to suggest anything. Certain departments had to do their work. I don't know what exactly was done or was ascertained. This was merely an assumption of mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would there have been any good reasons for this assumption rather than another one, that is, that the car did not belong to the police officer and that for that reason he should have been further prosecuted or that further disciplinary proceedings should be -- should have followed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I truly cannot recollect that anymore. I cannot remember the details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What do you remember apart from -- if you say you do not recollect the details anymore, what do you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember pulling him over -- actually, we met somewhere along the road. This was a policeman from my force, although I didn't know him personally. In any case, he was handed over to the employees of the Knin police station. And the request for a disciplinary procedure did arrive later, although I do not recall when exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you are totally unfamiliar with the fact on whether it was finally established that the car did belong to this police officer or did not belong to this police officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not recall that, and I'm not familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I invite you then to refrain from further assumptions which have a certain suggestive -- can have a certain suggestive impact. Ms. Mahindaratne, are you ready to cross-examine Mr. Cetina?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cetina, you will now be cross-examined by Ms. Mahindaratne. Ms. Mahindaratne is counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Cetina.

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I just wanted to clarify a couple of matters. In your statements to the Office of the Prosecutor as well as the Defence, you record your current occupation as police officer. Can you be a bit more specific. What is your current designation and in which department of the Ministry of the Interior are you working?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I work in the crime police administration on white-collar crime.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And what is your current designation?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am an assistant to the chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, yesterday we were discussing the Kotar-Knin Police Administration and the Knin-Zadar Police Administration. Just to clarify further, was the territory covered by the Kotar-Knin Police Administration within your area of responsibility, within the territory that was covered by the Knin-Zadar Police Administration?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So, in effect, the head of the Kotar-Knin Police Administration, Mr. Romanic, was subordinated to you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could explain it as follows: Formally speaking, he was subordinated to me, but the Kotar-Knin Police Administration had a special status vis-a-vis the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Okay. And one further clarification. Now, Mr. Bitanga was the head of uniformed police within your police administration; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And subordinated to you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, yesterday, Mr. Kay showed you some orders issued by the assistant minister of interior, Mr. Moric, regarding contacting military police between -- to co-operation. And you testified that it was Mr. Bitanga who contacted the military police in the area, and I'm referring to transcript page 23.404 to 05. Now, in addition to Mr. Bitanga, did you yourself also contact military police or commanders of the military police in your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, during several meetings, perhaps once or twice.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So it's once or twice that you contacted military police commanders in your area of responsibility during the -- during 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, yes. Mr. Bitanga had more operational contacts.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And who in the military police did you contact?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall Mr. Matanic fairly well, but not the others.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Have you met Colonel Budimir?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall Mr. Budimir.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Cetina, you were interviewed by the Defence in April of this year, which is the statement actually you, in fact, signed in August; isn't that correct? You signed the statement given to the Defence as a consequence to being interviewed in April of this year; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave a statement. I don't know when we established contact for the first time, but I signed the statement after I had given it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Were you interviewed only once or several times?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Twice, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Was the initial interview conducted in April 2009?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I no longer recall, although I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: There's no issue about that. My question is: At the time you were interviewed by the Defence, were you provided the statement that you had given to the Office of the Prosecutor to review?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And having reviewed the statement given to the Office of the Prosecutor, you, in fact, confirmed its accuracy when you made the statement to the Defence; isn't that correct? And let me, in fact, read what you have said in paragraph 1 of the Defence statement. This is D1743. You start off by saying: "I confirm that the statements which I gave to the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY on 10th and 11th September, 2001, and on 25th and 26th February, 2002, are true to the best of my recollection." Now, my question is -- what I'm getting at is this: Having said that, during the last two weeks when you were interviewed, that is, on the 13th and 23rd of October, you made three further corrections to the statement given to the Office of the Prosecutor. Now, how is it that you did not note those mistakes in the statement given to the Office of the Prosecutor initially when you reviewed it, when you were interviewed by the Defence in April this year?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were clarifications of certain answers.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Let me take you to those clarifications.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if you could call up D1744.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And this is a correction you made. You -- I'm going to the first clarification that is on page 1 of both versions. Referring to page 6, paragraph 4 of the -- your statement to the OTP, you made a correction to the paragraph that starts with: "I did not have any special contacts with the Croatian army. The only contact I had with the military was with General Ivan Cermak." And your clarification is this, you say -- you had said that you could not explain why this passage in this statement was written this way. "He had many contacts with the military police with whom he liaised both before Operation Oluja and after Operation Oluja." And you go on to clarify it further. And you go on to say: "Problems that he had experienced with military personnel committing offences within Zadar-Knin PU area he raised directly with the VP and his officers liaised directly with the commanders regularly." Now, you just said, Mr. Cetina, that you met the military police only twice, and most of the contacts were carried out by Mr. Bitanga, yet in your clarification you start off by saying that you had many contacts with the military police with whom you liaised both before Operation Oluja and after Operation Oluja. Now, can you explain to the Trial Chamber as to why suddenly during the last two weeks you decided to make that clarification or change to the OTP statement, having confirmed its accuracy when you were initially interviewed by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What this is all about is that I was, throughout this time, referring to the contacts that I and my associates had. I had far fewer contacts than they did, and that's what I tried to clarify here. It would have been far easier to have in front of me now the question that was put to me and in response to which I gave the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Let's go to the second correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If we could move, Mr. Registrar, to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And there you have made a correction to page 10 of the statement given to the OTP and paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Actually, that paragraph starts from page 9, Mr. Registrar, if you could just start with page 9 -- I'm sorry -- I'm sorry, I made a mistake, Mr. Registrar. We'll keep on this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In your statement given to the OTP, Mr. Cetina, you say this: "I do not know if any special commission was set up to investigate the murders in Varivode and Gosici. My only interest was to solve the cases in respect of ongoing crimes. I can say that we did a lot of things. We tried to process every important criminal act." And then after a couple of sentences you say: "I would agree that once the Serbs had fled from the liberated area, the area was under the control of the Croatian armed forces." And having said that, then you corrected that last couple of weeks in this way. You say that he had not said that particular sentence or that passage to the investigators in the context of this paragraph.
